notes: §1985:XI.4.4.4 GR10 defines the output procedure's range dynamically (statements reached by CALL, EXIT, GO TO, PERFORM, and declaratives executed from it) and says 'The range of the output procedure must not cause the execution of any MERGE, RELEASE, or SORT statement', a run-time prohibition with no stated result; §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR1 lets a SORT 'appear anywhere in the Procedure Division except in the declarative portion'. The range half conforms: CobolSort.EnterProcedure/ReturnStatement track the phase, so a RETURN reached by PERFORM outside the section (witness: AAA BBB CCC DONE) or from a USE procedure fired inside the range (probe declrange: USE-RETURNED BBB) works, and an executed RELEASE/SORT/MERGE in the range gets CobolSort's EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE net when checking is on (undefined at 85, so any result conforms; relinout ran AAA AFTER-REL BBB DONE). The defect is the compile-time half: VersionConformancePass.GateSortMergeProcedures reports COBOL2700 for a file SORT WRITTEN in an input or output procedure at EVERY edition (§2023:14.9.40.3 SR3), so a 1985 program whose output procedure holds a SORT that is never executed is refused (probes c3/sortinout, sortinip: COBOL2700 at 85). MERGE there is gated only from 2023 and is accepted at 85 (mergeinout: AAA BBB DONE), the correct 1985 answer; table SORT is refused at 85 by COBOL0870 (tablesort). Probes: b) sortinout/sortinip/mergeinout; c) tablesort; e) declrange with a failed OPEN (FS=35) whose USE procedure RETURNs; range via PERFORM (relinout, witness). kb/Work PB5274 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-pipe/slice-46.json).

next.reason: The range definition and ban are kept. 1985 'must not' states no result; 2023: 'If the range of the output procedure causes the execution of any MERGE, RELEASE, or format 1 SORT statement, the EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE exception condition is set to exist' and the SORT results are undefined (§2023:14.9.40.4 GR13); a RELEASE there also sets EC-FLOW-RELEASE (§2023:14.9.32.4 GR1). 2023 also refuses at compile time a SORT written 'in an input or output procedure' (§2023:14.9.40.3 SR3) and a MERGE written in 'an input or output procedure of a file format SORT statement' (§2023:14.9.24.3 SR1); 1985 SR1 allowed both outside declaratives. The format 1 limit only exempts the new table SORT.
